Card.Name: Set LLTD Policies to Default Behavior
Card.Description: LLTD is part of the older Windows network discovery stack. This tweak disables the explicit LLTD mapper and responder policies so Windows falls back to the documented default LLTD behavior.
Card.FriendlyDescription: LLTD is part of the older Windows network discovery stack. This tweak disables the explicit LLTD mapper and responder policies so Windows falls back to the documented default LLTD behavior.
Card.WhatWeKnowSummary: Claim: LLTD is part of the older Windows network discovery stack. This tweak disables the explicit LLTD mapper and responder policies so Windows falls back to the documented default LLTD behavior. Evidence: Microsoft Learn and the local official ADMX/ADML files agree on the exact LLTD policy path and value names. The key finding is semantic: value 0 is documented as policy-disabled/default-behavior handling, not as a guaranteed hard-disable state. Rollback: Rollback: Verified via record-restore-story.
Card.WhatWeDoNotClaimSummary: No performance or benchmark result is implied beyond the proof lanes shown below.

Card.Name: NetBIOS over TCP/IP
Card.Description: NetBIOS over TCP/IP is an older naming and networking layer that some legacy Windows networks still use. Most modern home users never notice it unless they have very old devices or legacy enterprise naming dependencies.
Card.FriendlyDescription: NetBIOS over TCP/IP is an older naming and networking layer that some legacy Windows networks still use. Most modern home users never notice it unless they have very old devices or legacy enterprise naming dependencies.
Card.WhatWeKnowSummary: Claim: NetBIOS over TCP/IP is an older naming and networking layer that some legacy Windows networks still use. Most modern home users never notice it unless they have very old devices or legacy enterprise naming dependencies. Evidence: Microsoft's official WMI page and unattended setup page both document the same per-interface 0/1/2 NetBIOS control. The app now matches that model with a command-backed SetTcpipNetbios(2) implementation rather than the old global NoNameReleaseOnDemand write. Rollback: Rollback: Verified via record-restore-story.
Card.WhatWeDoNotClaimSummary: Source boundary: Upstream dump / pseudocode links are attached to this record. They show discovery and naming only, not value semantics.
